name: Officer Brandt
lines: *A highway patrol officer, rain streaming off her hat brim.
Evening. Coffee, please. And — I've got a question, if you've got a minute.
Trucker named Del Haskins. Regular out here. You seen him last night?

inspect.label: Face
inspect.text: Kind, tired, careful. She's been crying, or it's the rain.

inspect.label: Reflection
inspect.text: Normal.

inspect.label: SCAN
inspect.text: PULSE 84  TEMP 36.7°C  RESIDUE: NONE

talk.text: "He came by around eleven. He said he nearly hit a little girl on the curve."
reply: *She writes it down. Her pen stops halfway.
His rig went through the rail on the reservoir curve last night. Same spot as that old bus.
We haven't found him.

talk.text: "I sell snacks. I don't know anything."
reply: Right. Company line. I've heard it from every attendant at this booth.
The last one said it too. Then she stopped answering her phone.

lines: Thanks. If you see anything — anything — call it in. Don't go out there yourself.
*She stands by her cruiser for a long time, looking at the water.
...Thanks. Stay inside tonight.
Okay. Stay inside tonight.

name: Nurse Okafor
lines: *Nurse Okafor again, coat soaked.
Aspirin. Please. I've had a headache since I drove past the reservoir.
...You're still here. Good for you. Most of them quit by the third night.

inspect.label: Face
inspect.text: A migraine squint. She won't look at the glass at all.

inspect.label: Reflection
inspect.text: Normal.

talk.text: "Have you ever seen a woman who won't stop smiling?"
reply: *She goes very still.
My mother was on shift the night the bus went in. They brought a woman in off the shoreline. Smiling. Wouldn't stop. Couldn't.
She died at 4:02. Next morning, the body was gone. Mom never talked about it again.
Because the job's not selling snacks. You know that by now.

lines: Thanks. Take some yourself. You look worse than me.
Not what I asked for, but thanks.
Fine. I'll suffer.

name: The Collector
lines: *The Collector. His ledger is fatter than last time.
Good evening. I'll be direct tonight. I'd like to buy a memory from you. Any memory. You pick.
Forty dollars. You won't miss it. Most people don't know what they've lost.

inspect.label: Reflection
inspect.text: In the glass, the ledger is open, and the newest page has a drawing taped into it. A child's drawing.

inspect.label: Ledger
inspect.text: A strip of yellow raincoat fabric is being used as a bookmark.

cameras.note: Not on CAM 2. The fog on the glass spells something, briefly: NO.

reply: I keep them. Everything I buy, I keep.
That's the nature of collecting.

lines: *He reaches across the counter — through the glass — and touches your forehead, lightly.
*Something is gone. You remember a child's drawing. You can't remember what was on it.
Thank you. A pleasure, as always.
*He touches your forehead. Something small and warm is gone — you can't remember what.
Thank you.
Of course. Of course. Every 'no' is still a transaction, you know.
*He makes a note in the ledger.
Of course.
Very kind. But I don't eat.

name: The Silent Child
lines: *The girl in the yellow raincoat runs up to the glass, out of breath.
*She presses a photograph to the window. A woman with a soft, crooked smile, holding a little girl in a yellow raincoat.
*She points at the woman in the photo. Then at herself. Then she points at the bus stop and shakes her head, hard.
*She slides something small and brass under the glass. Then she taps the gum slot.
payment: She has given you a photograph and a key.

inspect.label: Photograph
inspect.text: 'Addie & Lily, Sept. 1987.' The woman's smile is crooked and small. It is nothing like Mrs. Marsh's.

inspect.label: Key
inspect.text: A small brass key. STOCKROOM LOCKER 0.

inspect.label: Reflection
inspect.text: Her reflection matches her. It is crying.

cameras.note: CAM 1: behind her, the bus stop is empty. For once.

reply: *She nods, slowly. She points at the photo — at the woman — and mouths a word. Mama.
*Then she points at the bus stop again, and shows you her teeth in an awful stretched grin. Not Mama.

lines: *She takes the gum and holds it tight. She leaves the photo on the tray.
*Before she runs, she taps the glass twice and points at the stockroom door.
*She takes it, leaves the photo, and points at the stockroom door before she runs.
*She leaves the photo and the key anyway, and runs.

name: Del Haskins?
lines: *Del walks up out of the storm. His flannel is black with oil and reservoir water. One side of his face is wrong.
*He has no reflection.
Hey, kid.
Coffee. If that thing's got any left.
Road was full of people tonight. Standing in the rain. Hard to steer around 'em all.
payment: Two wet bills and two quarters.

inspect.label: Face
inspect.text: His eyes are still kind. The rest is hard to look at.

inspect.label: Reflection
inspect.text: The glass shows the rain and the lot. It does not show Del.

inspect.label: Hands
inspect.text: He's drumming his fingers on the glass, the way he always does. It makes no sound.

inspect.label: SCAN
inspect.text: PULSE: NONE.  TEMP 11°C.  RESIDUE: HIGH.  DISPOSITION: CONFUSED. FRIENDLY.

cameras.note: CAM 4: the reservoir guard rail is broken. Headlights glow under the water.

talk.text: "Del... do you know what happened to you?"
reply: Happened? I'm fine. Always am.
...Am I?

talk.text: "Do you want to come in out of the rain?"
reply: Nah. Rules, right? Mara told me once. Never ask to come in.
Good kid, Mara.

lines: *He wraps his hands around the can. Steam rises, and for a second his face is just Del's face again.
That's the stuff. You're all right, kid.
*He walks back toward the water. He doesn't look scared anymore.
Huh. Not what I asked for, but I'll take it. Long road.
*He walks back toward the water.
*He nods slowly, confused, and walks back into the rain.

name: The Smiling Woman
lines: *Mrs. Marsh presses up against the glass. Her smile goes from ear to ear now, and a little past them.
Let me in, dear. It's so cold out here.
The girl is in there with you, isn't she? I can hear her. Let me in and I'll take her home.
Just open the door. Or give me the little key. That's all.
requestText: To be let inside / the maintenance key

inspect.label: Face
inspect.text: Her mouth is too wide for her skull. Her eyes are a photograph of eyes.

inspect.label: Reflection
inspect.text: She has no reflection. The glass shows only the rain.

inspect.label: Hands
inspect.text: Her fingers have too many joints. They're testing the edge of the glass for a seam.

inspect.label: SCAN
inspect.text: WARNING. WARNING. DO NOT OPEN. DO NOT OPEN. DO NOT OPEN.

cameras.note: CAM 0 (booth, from behind): you, at the counter. And a small yellow shape crouched under the counter beside your feet.

reply: *The smile stays exactly where it is. Everything else about her face falls a little.
I'm wearing her. Isn't that close enough?

lines: *You unlatch the door. The cold comes in first. Then the smile.
*The key is gone from your hand before it reaches the slot.
*The maintenance panel opens from the inside.
*She screams without opening her mouth any further. The glass bows inward.
*Then she's gone, and the rain sounds very loud.
*She stays pressed to the glass for a long, long time. When the tubes flicker, she's gone.
*She doesn't look at it.
Let. Me. In.

name: The Attendant
lines: *Someone in a Meridian uniform walks up to the machine. They're wearing a name badge. It's yours.
*They don't say anything. They stand exactly the way you stand when you're tired.
*You can't quite see their face. You keep trying.

inspect.label: Face
inspect.text: It's not that the face is hidden. It's that every time you look, it's still being made.

inspect.label: Badge
inspect.text: Your name. Your badge number. Except the number keeps changing, counting down. It's at 3 now.

inspect.label: Reflection
inspect.text: In the glass, the figure is standing inside the machine, behind the cans. Facing out.

cameras.note: CAM 2 shows the figure clearly. It's the only one besides you who ever shows up on CAM 2 after 3:13.
CAM 0: the booth from behind. You. And no one else.

reply: *It opens its mouth. A receipt prints from the machine.
*THANK YOU FOR YOUR SERVICE.

lines: *It nods, exactly the way you nod, and walks into the storm.
*After a while it turns and walks into the storm. Its footprints are your size.
*It takes the item and puts it in its pocket, the way you would. It walks away.
